newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean, Mexican presidents agree to boost trade.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean, Mexican presidents agree to boost trade.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam and Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo agreed on Friday to promote trade and cooperation between their nations.
The two leaders also witnessed the signing of an extradition treaty and a protocol on tourism cooperation after a meeting held at the presidential Blue House, Kim's aides said.
"The two presidents have agreed to expand bilateral trade in view of their complementary economies," a Blue House official said.
South Korean exports to Mexico totalled $940 million in calendar 1995, against imports worth $310 million, according to Seoul figures.
Zedillo, the first Mexican head of state to visit South Korea since the two countries established diplomatic ties in 1962, arrived in Seoul on Thursday for a three-day visit.
The Mexican leader asked Kim to help encourage South Korean companies to invest in his country, the official said.

On Friday, South Korea's Export-Import Bank granted a $10 million credit line to Mexico's trade development bank, Banco Comercio Exterior (Bancomext), to promote technology transfers and the import of South Korean capital goods to Mexico.
A memorandum of cooperation was also signed on Friday between the Electronics Industries Association of Korea and its Mexican counterpart, CANIECE, association officials said.
A Seoul Foreign Ministry statement said investments in Mexico by South Korean companies would total $800 million by the end of this year.
Zedillo's trip to South Korea is the last leg of his Asian visit, which took him to Beijing, Singapore and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Manila.
